messages:
morgan: Quick report — found a reproducible duplication of request body for streaming uploads when our Kotlin retrofit adapter retries after an auth refresh. Happens on Android 13+ devices and emulator.

eli: ugh. does it reproduce with plain okhttp + retrofit without our call adapter?

morgan: no, plain retrofit + okhttp (synchronous call) is fine. repro is with OurCoroutineCallAdapter + RetryInterceptor + TokenAuthenticator. Behavior: interceptor retries the request after 401, but the first call’s coroutine still reads remaining stream chunks and then the second call sends them again -> server sees repeated bytes.

sam: that sounds like request body not being repeatable. are we wrapping streaming body with BufferedSink or using RequestBody.create?

morgan: we stream via RequestBody with writeTo(sink) reading from an InputStream. We assumed our RetryInterceptor would only replay if body is repeatable, but Authenticator triggers a new call after failure and we don’t detect non-repeatable.

nora: which SDK version and example app?

morgan: sampleapp branch: devex/retry-stream-fix, SDK 0.11.3-alpha, okhttp 4.10.0 pinned in Gradle. Repro steps:
1) Start sampleapp upload streaming endpoint (large file generator)
2) Force early 401 by toggling backend auth simulator
3) Authenticator refreshes token and triggers new request
4) Observe server logs: duplicate sequence of bytes and Content-Length mismatch.

raj: maybe our coroutine adapter defers closing the original call’s body source so it continues draining. If we cancel coroutine on retry, the stream should stop. Does cancellation propagate?

morgan: cancellation does not fully propagate with our adapter; coroutine scope cancel only marks job but okhttp call still continues reading. I added `call.cancel()` in adapter on coroutine cancellation and it helps but then server sees a truncated request and we get partial uploads — worse.

eli: alternative: mark non-repeatable bodies with Request.tag and prevent Authenticator from replaying them. Authenticator can check for `request.tag("nonRepeatable")` and return null (do not retry) so the original failure surfaces. Safer than force-cancel.

sam: can we also add a wrapper that buffers up to N bytes to make small bodies repeatable and fallback to non-repeatable tag for large streams?

morgan: implemented a small-buffer wrapper in sampleapp and repro reduced duplication for files < 512KB. For large streams still non-repeatable. Pushed branch and logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/sampleapp/2751012345/stream-dup/logs.txt

ci-bot: :link: Build artifact uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/sampleapp/2751012345/stream-dup/logs.txt

nora: I'll add integration test that toggles auth mid-upload and asserts server saw single stream. Also adding flaky label.

raj: file bug DEVEX-3150 and propose two fixes: 1) defensive Authenticator check for non-repeatable tag, 2) improve adapter cancellation propagation + doc note about streaming bodies and repeatability.

morgan: filed DEVEX-3150 and referenced sampleapp branch. Will follow up with PR for Authenticator change.

eli: sanity check: update docs in SDK README about streaming body best practices and add example using BufferingRequestBody for small payloads.

sam: thanks — add a changelog entry if we backport to stable SDK.

morgan: will coordinate patch release if customers hit this in prod. Thanks all.
